notice.about: Every word the MCP endpoint shows a model: the tool names, their descriptions, their argument descriptions and their annotations. Read by the /mcp endpoint in this bundle.
notice.stability: Descriptions and inputSchema are published contract, not prose to tidy. Claude Desktop hashes a tool's description and parameters into the user's "always allow" grant, so revising wording silently revokes it. Change these words deliberately, in a release, on purpose.
notice.language: English only, and excluded from translation. This text is read by a model, not by the user.

fields.operationId, method, pathTemplate, bindi: routing, used only by the endpoint to dispatch into the REST routing table

tools.name: pp_list_files
tools.description: List the portfolio files this connector may address. Every other tool needs one of them as its `file`: send its `use` value exactly; a `label` or an `alias` is for display, never an address. Start here — there is no default file and no active file. Only files the user has open in Portfolio Performance *and* has individually enabled appear.

tools.name: pp_list_instruments
tools.description:
List every instrument in a file — what the application itself labels a *security*: stocks, funds, bonds, crypto, and currency-less series such as an index. Each entry is the complete record, identical to what pp_get_instrument returns, including any custom attributes that are set.

This is how a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker becomes the `uuid` that every other instrument tool requires - pass it as `query` to get just the matching instruments rather than the whole list, which in a large file is more than one answer can carry: it comes back one page at a time, and `page.nextOffset` says where the next one starts.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

query.description: Only the instruments this finds: one whose name contains it, or whose ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol equals it - ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. Omit it to list every instrument. Use it whenever the user names an instrument: a large file has more instruments than fit in one answer, and a query returns just the ones meant, each with its `uuid`.

cursor.description: Where a page continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before, exactly as given. Omit it to start at the first. A list too large for one answer comes back as its first page anyway, with `page.nextCursor` saying where the next one continues.

limit.description: At most this many instruments. Omit it for as many as fit in one answer.

tools.name: pp_get_instrument
tools.description:
Read one instrument by `uuid`: name, trading currency, ISIN, WKN, ticker symbol, note and custom attributes. The record is the same one pp_list_instruments carries, so reach for this when you already hold a `uuid` — off a holding, a trade or a performance row — and want the master data behind it rather than the whole file.

Custom attributes come back keyed by an opaque attribute `id`, never by the name the user sees in the application; pp_list_attribute_types is what puts a name to one. Only attributes that are actually set appear, and only those with a scalar type.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

tools.name: pp_create_instrument
tools.description:
Adds an instrument to the file: its name, its trading currency, and the identifiers the caller happens to have.

**No quote is fetched.** The application's own dialog asks a provider for quotes and identifiers when a user creates an instrument; a call that reached a provider in the background would cause a side effect the caller can neither see nor order. So this creates an instrument with no quote feed and no prices at all - the feed is set in the application, and master data afterwards with pp_update_instrument. That is the whole of what this tool will not do, and the reason it exists anyway: reaching for a name that is missing is otherwise a trip to the keyboard.

`name` and `currencyCode` are required in practice although no body property can be declared required: leave either out and the call comes back refused with the field named. A currency-less series - what an index is - is deliberately not created here, though the change tool can make an instrument one afterwards. Custom attributes can come along in the same call, keyed and typed exactly as in pp_update_instrument: those definitions belong to the file rather than to the instrument, so there is nothing to wait for.

**An identifier the file already carries is refused, and nothing is created.** If the ISIN or the WKN belongs to another instrument, the refusal names that instrument with its uuid. Two instruments answering to one ISIN send every later search for it to whichever the file happens to list first, which is a mess nobody asked for. A ticker symbol is not that kind of identifier - the same ticker is ordinary across share classes and trading venues - so a shared ticker is not a refusal: those instruments are listed under `sameTickerAs`, and the same is done for the name under `sameNameAs`. Both are absent when the file has nothing else like it.

The answer carries the instrument with its new `uuid`: unlike a watchlist this has an identifier, and that uuid is how every other instrument tool addresses it. `hasQuoteFeed` and `hasTransactions` say what the record cannot - nothing was fetched, nothing refers to it yet - and that last part is what makes this reversible: pp_delete_instrument removes the instrument again for as long as no transaction and no investment plan uses it, which is the one real undo in this API.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the instrument as it will be called: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. A request that cannot be carried out is refused before anybody is asked about it. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: What the instrument is to be called. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused naming this field. Must not be blank.

currencyCode.description: The trading currency as an ISO 4217 code, e.g. EUR. Required in practice, and refused if the file has no series to that currency - prices are read in this currency.

isin.description: Twelve characters with a correct check digit, checked as the application checks it. Refused if another instrument already carries it.

wkn.description: The German securities identifier. Refused if another instrument already carries it.

tickerSymbol.description: The ticker symbol. Unlike ISIN and WKN this may repeat across the file - then the instruments sharing it are listed under `sameTickerAs`.

note.description: Free text shown with the instrument.

attributes.description: Optional, and shaped exactly as in pp_update_instrument: custom attributes keyed by the opaque attribute `id` from pp_list_attribute_types, with a value of the type declared there. The attribute definitions belong to the file, not to the instrument, so they can be set while the instrument is being created.

tools.name: pp_update_instrument
tools.description:
Change an instrument's master data or its custom attributes. This is a merge, not a replacement: only the arguments you pass are touched, and passing null clears a field rather than setting it blank. Nothing else about an instrument is writable here — prices, transactions, quote feeds, events and taxonomies are read-only, and an instrument that does not exist yet is made by pp_create_instrument, not here. Nothing is saved to disk - closing the file without saving discards the change, and there is no other undo. A patch is checked in full before anything is written, so it applies completely or not at all. A patch that names no field this API can write changes nothing: the response is the instrument as it already stands, and the file is not marked dirty.

Custom attributes are addressed by the opaque attribute `id` from pp_list_attribute_types, never by the display name, and each value has to match the type declared there. The types: `string` and `boolean` as JSON strings and booleans; `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD`; `amount`, `quote` and `shares` as plain decimal numbers in currency units or shares (`1234.56`, not scaled); and the two numeric types to mind - a `percent` value is a fraction, so 0.7% is `0.007`, while a `number` value is unscaled, so an attribute the application reads as a percentage takes `5` to mean 5%. A patch that only restates values the instrument already has changes nothing and does not mark the file dirty.

While the user has a dialog open in the application, or is part-way through editing a cell, writes are refused until they finish. That is normal and temporary, not a request that went wrong.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user about it. A no answers `403 write-declined` and it stands - asking again will not change it. Nobody answering within two minutes answers `423 write-unanswered`, and since nothing was changed it can be tried again. While another change is still waiting for an answer this one is refused as `429 write-pending`. The user may also allow further calls of this kind without being asked again. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

name.description: A new display name. Must be non-empty and cannot be cleared; omit it to leave the name alone.

currencyCode.description: A new trading currency as an ISO 4217 code, or null to remove it and mark the instrument a currency-less series such as an index. Any currency change, clearing included, is refused once the instrument has transactions — the same rule the application applies. It is likewise refused on an instrument that carries an exchange rate, whose rate series depends on the two currencies.

isin.description: A new ISIN, or null to clear it. Omit to leave it as it is. Checked like the application checks it: twelve characters with a matching check digit, or the whole call fails.

wkn.description: A new WKN, the German securities identifier, or null to clear it. Omit to leave it as it is.

tickerSymbol.description: A new ticker symbol, or null to clear it. Omit to leave it as it is.

note.description: A new free-text note, or null to clear it. Omit to leave it as it is.

attributes.description:
Custom attributes to change, keyed by the opaque attribute `id` from pp_list_attribute_types — never by the name shown in the application. A value sets that attribute, null clears it, and any id you leave out is untouched. Every value has to match the attribute's declared type; an unknown id, a compound type this connector cannot write, or a mistyped value fails the whole call rather than being quietly skipped.

An attribute of type `image` — the application's **logo** — takes a PNG as base64, with or without the `data:image/png;base64,` prefix, at most 64 KiB of bytes; it is stored in the data-url form the application renders from, and it is never read back, so the successful write and `changed` are your confirmation. When you need a company's icon, look first at **companieslogo.com** — PNGs, usually one light and one dark variant, take the one that suits the application's appearance — and only then elsewhere, e.g. the company's own newsroom. Take the **icon/symbol** variant, never the full-size logo: the wide wordmark is exactly what the 64 KiB cap refuses, while a 128 px icon fits many times over. This connector fetches nothing: get the file yourself, then hand its bytes over. An attribute of type `limit-price` takes the string `"<=62.5"`: one of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and a price with a dot as decimal separator, in the instrument's own currency; it reads back in exactly that form.

tools.name: pp_delete_instrument
tools.description:
Delete an instrument from a file. Refused outright while any transaction or investment plan still refers to it. Erasing it would take that history with it, and this connector will not make that call on the user's behalf — they have to clear the transactions, or take the instrument out of the investment plan, first; a refusal says which of the two applies. A successful delete names the instrument it removed. Sitting in a watchlist or a taxonomy does not block a delete. Like every write here it is not saved to disk: closing the file without saving brings the instrument back, and there is no other undo.

Like any write, this is refused while the user has a dialog open in the application. That is temporary, not a failure.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

tools.name: pp_list_attribute_types
tools.description:
List the custom attribute definitions that apply to instruments in a file: each one's opaque `id`, the name the user sees, and its value type. Attributes are defined per file, and everywhere else they are addressed by that `id` — a display name is never accepted — so read this before setting one with pp_update_instrument, and to put a name to an attribute id read off an instrument.

The types matter when writing. `percent` values are fractions, so `0.007` is 0.7%, while `number` values are unscaled, so `5` in an attribute the application reads as a percentage means 5%. The compound types differ: a `limit-price` reads and writes as a compact string — one of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` and a dot-decimal price, like `"<=62.5"` — an image is writable (`writable: true`) yet never read back (`supported: false`), set through pp_update_instrument as base64 PNG where a source for company logos is suggested too, and a bookmark is neither (`supported: false`, `writable: false`).

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

tools.name: pp_list_instrument_prices
tools.description:
The stored price history of one instrument: its quotes day by day, oldest first and the newest last - the series the price chart draws and the positions are valued from. Reach for it whenever the question is how a series moved: an instrument record carries no price at all, and a holding names only the single price its own valuation rests on.

The series includes the instrument's latest quote even when a feed fetched it and it was never stored as history, because that is the quote a valuation rests on. There is no `order`: pages run forward only, so a caller after the recent end of a long series narrows `from` instead of walking everything. `count`, `firstDate` and `lastDate` describe the whole window, not the page. An instrument without a single stored price answers with an empty list, not an error.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

from.description: First day of the window, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. Without it, no lower bound.

to.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. Without it, no upper bound; never before `from`.

cursor.description: Where a page continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before. It names this instrument and this window, so a cursor from another is refused rather than quietly skipping prices.

limit.description: At most this many prices; omit it for as many as fit in one answer. A long series is large: an index held for decades is tens of thousands of quotes.

tools.name: pp_update_quotes
tools.description:
Starts the application's own price update - the job behind its *Update quotes* menu item - for a chosen part of the file.

Nothing is fetched here and no provider is picked here. Each instrument keeps the feed the application configured for it, the update runs in the application with its own progress dialog and its own error reporting, and the application itself marks the file unsaved as quotes arrive. What this call settles is the scope - and it is asked about first, like every change here.

`scope` chooses the part of the file. `all` (the default) hands over the whole file the way the plain menu item does, indices and exchange rates along with the instruments. `active` takes every instrument not set to retired. `instrument` takes exactly the one named by `instrument`. `watchlist` takes the instruments of the list named by `watchlist`. Holdings are deliberately not a scope of their own: the menu's version of that resolves them through a valuation, which no part of this call has a use for.

The answer is `202`, and it describes what was **started**, not what arrived: `securities` in scope, `withQuoteFeed` of those reachable by a feed, `started: true`. The update runs on past this call - either watch the application's own progress dialog, or read pp_list_instrument_prices afterwards to see what came in. `X-Portfolio-Changed` answers whether the file can end up unsaved: `false` when nothing in scope has a feed that could deliver anything, and `true` for `all`, which takes exchange rates with it.

Refused with `400`, before anyone is asked, when `scope` is not one of the four, when `instrument` names no uuid or the file does not have it, when `watchlist` names nothing or no list of that name, or when the body carries a field this call does not read.

Before it starts, the application asks the user, naming the scope: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was started, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer.

This is the one tool of the API that reaches out to the internet, which is exactly why the user is asked. Sending it twice fetches twice.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

scope.description: Which part of the file to refresh: `all` the whole file as the menu item does (default), `active` every instrument not set to retired, `instrument` the one named by `instrument`, `watchlist` the instruments of the list named by `watchlist`.

instrument.description: The uuid of the one instrument to refresh, from pp_list_instruments. Only read when scope is `instrument`; refused as `400` when that scope is chosen without it, or with a uuid the file does not have.

watchlist.description: The name of the watchlist whose instruments to refresh, spelled as pp_list_watchlists names it. Only read when scope is `watchlist`; refused as `400` when that scope is chosen without it, or with a name the file does not have.

tools.name: pp_list_cash_accounts
tools.description: Every cash account in a file — the accounts holding money in a single currency, which the application itself calls simply *accounts*. Each entry gives the `uuid`, name, currency and note — and no balance. What an account is actually worth on a given day comes from pp_list_holdings, which values cash and instrument positions side by side.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

tools.name: pp_get_cash_account
tools.description: Read one cash account by `uuid`: its name, its currency and its note. It carries no balance — pp_list_holdings is where a cash account's value on a date comes from. The record is the same one pp_list_cash_accounts returns, so reach for this when you already hold a `uuid` and want the name behind it: typically the `referenceCashAccount` of an investment account, or a cash line in a statement of assets.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The cash account's `uuid`, from pp_list_cash_accounts — or read off an investment account's `referenceCashAccount`, or a `cash-account` holding.

tools.name: pp_create_cash_account
tools.description:
Adds one cash account to the file - what the application itself calls simply an *account*: money in a single currency, and the money end of every structure a caller might build.

`name` is required in practice although no body property can be declared required: leave it out and the call comes back `400` naming the field. `currencyCode` may be left out and then takes the file's own base currency; given, it has to be a currency the file already moves in - the base currency, or one an instrument or account carries - because prices and reports read their rates from series the file holds, and a currency outside them is refused as `unknown-currency` naming the currencies it does move in.

A name the file already carries, in the very same currency, is refused as `409 name-taken` naming the account that holds it. An account does have a uuid, so two of one name could be told apart - but only by a caller that went and looked, which is the mistake this refuses to let through quietly. Another currency makes another account, and that pair is ordinary.

The answer carries the account with its new `uuid`, which every other account tool addresses by. Nothing is saved to disk: closing the file without saving discards the account, and there is no other undo - this API creates accounts and never removes one.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the account and its currency: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: What the account is to be called. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused naming this field.

currencyCode.description: The currency the account holds, as an ISO 4217 code, e.g. EUR. Optional: left out it is the file's base currency. Must be a currency the file moves in.

note.description: Free text shown with the account.

tools.name: pp_list_investment_accounts
tools.description: Every investment account in a file — securities accounts, which the application calls *portfolios*. An investment account holds instrument positions and nothing else; the money that goes with it sits in an ordinary cash account, whose uuid it carries as `referenceCashAccount`. A user asking what is "in an account" usually means the two together, so read the cash side as well before answering.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

tools.name: pp_get_investment_account
tools.description: Read one investment account by `uuid`: its name, its note, and the `referenceCashAccount` where the money that belongs with it is kept — the account itself holds instrument positions and nothing else. The record is the same one pp_list_investment_accounts returns, so reach for this when you already hold a `uuid`, such as the securities account named on a trade.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The investment account's `uuid`, from pp_list_investment_accounts — or read off the `portfolio` named on a trade.

tools.name: pp_create_investment_account
tools.description:
Adds one investment account to the file - a securities account, which the application calls a *portfolio*. A depot holds instrument positions and nothing else: the money that belongs with it lives in its **reference cash account**, and every purchase booked into the depot draws its money from that account. Creating a depot without settling its money is how a file ends up with two brokers and no way to tell whose cash paid.

So `referenceCashAccount` matters: the uuid of a cash account from pp_list_cash_accounts. Left out, it must be the file's one cash account in the base currency - and if the file holds none or several, the call is refused rather than guessed, asking for the uuid.

`name` is required in practice although no body property can be declared required: leave it out and the call comes back `400` naming the field. A name another depot already carries is refused as `409 name-taken` naming that depot - depots have uuids, but a caller that had made two of one name could not know which one it had made.

The answer carries the depot with its new `uuid` and its `referenceCashAccount`. Nothing is saved to disk: closing the file without saving discards it, and there is no other undo - this API creates depots and never removes one.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the depot and the money account it will point at: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: What the depot is to be called. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused naming this field.

referenceCashAccount.description: The uuid of the cash account that belongs with this depot, from pp_list_cash_accounts. Optional: left out, the file's one cash account in its base currency is used - and if there is not exactly one, the call asks for the uuid.

note.description: Free text shown with the depot.

tools.name: pp_get_file_info
tools.description:
The file itself, in the cheapest answer this API gives: the currency it counts in, every currency it moves in, the version its XML was read at, and how many of each kind of thing it holds.

Worth reading before anything larger, when a file is not known yet: the counts say whether `pp_list_holdings` will hold a handful of positions or a thousand, and whether there are taxonomies at all before `pp_list_taxonomies` is a question worth asking. `baseCurrency` is the currency every report defaults to; `currencies` are the ones the accounts, portfolios and instruments actually use, so a `reportingCurrency` outside that list converts at 1:1 and names itself in `fxWarnings`.

The counts are an inventory, not a statement of assets: an instrument with no position still counts, and so does a closed account - what is owned and what it is worth on a date is `pp_list_holdings`. `fileVersion` is the format version the file was read at, not a modification date, and it says nothing about a newer copy on disk.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

tools.name: pp_list_watchlists
tools.description:
The watchlists of a file: named baskets of instruments that the application quotes together. A watchlist is not an account and holds nothing - it is a selection of names, the answer to which instruments one keeps an eye on - and it is the one thing in a file without an identifier: `name` is all a reader can quote back, and no uuid anywhere points at a list.

By default each list only says how full it is (`instrumentCount`); `withInstruments=true` adds the instruments as `{uuid, name}` pairs, which is worth asking for only together with `instrument`, because a working list carries several hundred and this answer is never paged. `instrument` narrows to the lists holding that one instrument - how to ask where a name is kept without pulling every list of the file along.

A watchlist says nothing about ownership: an instrument can be watched without being held, and held without being watched. What is owned and what it is worth is `pp_list_holdings`. When nothing comes back, `empty` says whether the file has no watchlists at all or only none holding what was asked for - two different answers that an empty list cannot tell apart.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

instrument.description: Only the lists holding this one instrument, as its `uuid` from pp_list_instruments. The answer then names the lists, not just the instrument.

withInstruments.description: Whether each list also carries the instruments it holds. Off by default: a working list holds several hundred, and `instrumentCount` states the size either way.

tools.name: pp_create_watchlist
tools.description:
Adds a watchlist to the file, optionally already holding instruments.

A watchlist has **no identifier**: its name is the only way to address it, and no uuid anywhere in the file points at one. That answers a question here that no other object of the file asks. A name already in use is refused as `409 name-taken` rather than created, because once two lists share a name nothing this API returns can tell them apart. Names are compared exactly once the spaces around them are gone, and not folded to one case - `Tech` and `tech` are two lists, and the second one is refused only against a list already named `tech`.

`name` is required in practice even though a body property cannot be declared required: leave it out and the call comes back `400` naming the field. The name travels in the body rather than in the path for the same reason it has no uuid - a list name is free text, free text can hold a slash, and a path segment cannot be asked to survive one.

`instruments` takes uuids as pp_list_instruments gives them. One that is not in the file refuses the whole request instead of adding the rest, because a caller that meant to add two names and got one would never hear of it. A list with no instruments is not a failure: that is what the application calls an empty watchlist, and pp_update_watchlist fills it.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the list: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: What the list is to be called, as the navigation will show it. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused with a 400 naming this field. Refused with `409 name-taken` if the file already has a list of that very name.

instruments.description: Uuids of the instruments the list should hold, from pp_list_instruments. Omit it for an empty list. Any uuid the file does not have refuses the whole request.

tools.name: pp_update_watchlist
tools.description:
Puts instruments into one watchlist and takes others out of it, both in one request - so moving a name from one list to another costs one call, and the surface does not grow a tool per direction.

`name` says which list, and is required in practice although a body property cannot be declared required: omitted, the call comes back `400` naming the field. A list the file does not have is refused as `409 no-such-watchlist`, and the refusal names the lists the file does have. As everywhere a watchlist is addressed, the name is in the body and not the path: it is free text, and free text can hold a slash.

Give at least one of `add` or `remove`. Both take uuids from pp_list_instruments, and a uuid the file does not have refuses the whole request rather than being skipped. Something listed under `remove` that the list does not hold is **not** an error - the state asked for already holds - and comes back under `notHeld`, which is what makes this request safe to send twice. Adding a name the list already holds does nothing at all, as the model keeps a list free of duplicates.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the list: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: Which list to change, spelled as pp_list_watchlists names it. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused with a 400 naming this field.

add.description: Uuids to put into the list, from pp_list_instruments. One already in the list is left as it is.

remove.description: Uuids to take out of the list. Only the selection goes: the instrument itself stays in the file. Uuids the list does not hold are reported under `notHeld` rather than refused.

tools.name: pp_delete_watchlist
tools.description:
Takes one watchlist out of the file. `name` says which one, spelled exactly as pp_list_watchlists names it, and travels in the body as it does for creating and changing a list: a list has no uuid, its name is the only address, and free text can hold a slash a path segment cannot survive.

A list the file does not have is refused as `409 no-such-watchlist`, and the refusal names the lists the file does have - so sending this twice fails the second time, and there is no undo. Making the list again with pp_create_watchlist, under the very name and with the very instruments, is the way back.

What was watched stays: a watchlist only points at instruments, it does not hold them. Removing a list takes away a selection, never a security, and changes nothing about the holdings, the bookings, or the other lists the same names appear in.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the list: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

name.description: Which list to remove, spelled as pp_list_watchlists names it. Required in practice: omitted, the call is refused with a 400 naming this field.

tools.name: pp_get_category_performance
tools.description:
How one class of a taxonomy performed between two dates: the report of `pp_get_overall_performance` with its scope narrowed from the whole file to what one class holds - the same fields, the same signs, the same reconciliation.

What a class holds is the application's own reckoning and not merely the vehicles tagged to it: a cash account assigned to the class counts as money, and the settlement cash of a securities account is shared out between the classes its holdings belong to. The classes of one tree therefore add back up to the whole file - and an instrument's own row in `pp_list_instrument_performance` need not match its share of a class, because the cash belongs to the class and not to the instrument.

One class per call: `class` is its id from pp_list_taxonomies, unique within a taxonomy, so `taxonomy` is only needed when several taxonomies define that same id. A class holding nothing has no capital to measure a return on, so `ttwror` and `irr` come back null and not 0 %, while `category.assignedCount` states what the class holds. `category` names the class the figures belong to - id, name, parent and taxonomy - because a report over a class would otherwise carry nothing saying which one it is. The figures are computed for this request and stored nowhere: only the same dates and settings reproduce them.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

class.description: The class to report on, as its `id` from the classes of pp_list_taxonomies. Nothing else resolves: a class name is not an id, and the same name appears in several trees.

taxonomy.description: The taxonomy the class belongs to, as its `id`. Optional, because a class id is unique within one tree; only needed when several taxonomies define that same id, which is otherwise refused rather than guessed.

openingDate.description: Start of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD; a transaction on this day counts as part of the starting position.

closingDate.description: End of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, after the opening date; defaults to today. For a date in the future see pp_get_overall_performance.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings`.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`: the cost basis gains are measured against. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return.

tools.name: pp_list_investment_plans
tools.description:
The savings plans of a file: what it intends to book next, how often, and between which two accounts. Nothing else on this API speaks of the future - a holding states what is there and `pp_list_transactions` states what happened - so a plan is the one thing neither of them answers.

A plan is a schedule, not a booking. What it has already executed is ordinary transactions in the accounts it names, visible in `pp_list_transactions` like any other booking; this states how many (`executions`), the date of the last one and the date the next is due, but does not repeat them. `executions: 0` means the plan has never run, and then no `lastExecution` comes back at all; `nextExecution` is the date the application would use next - for a plan that never ran that is its `start`, which can lie in the past, and it does not move until something is generated. `interval` together with `intervalUnit` is the rhythm: `interval: 1` with `intervalUnit: month` is the monthly plan the application shows, `2` with `week` every second week. `amount` is the rate of one execution, `fees` and `taxes` appear only when the plan carries them.

`type` is what a plan does: `PURCHASE_OR_DELIVERY` buys or delivers into `investmentAccount`, `DEPOSIT` pays money into a cash account, `REMOVAL` takes money out, `INTEREST` books interest. A plan that buys names no cash account of its own - the `cashAccount` stated for it is the settlement account of its securities account, derived exactly as a purchase booking derives it. A plan is named, never identified: it has no uuid, and since plans cannot be written through this API there is nothing to point at. `investmentAccount`, `cashAccount` and `instrument` take a uuid and narrow the list; a file holds plans by the dozen, so this answer is never paged. When nothing comes back, `empty` says which kind of nothing it is - that the file holds no plans at all, or that none of its plans match what was asked for - because an empty list cannot tell the two apart and they lead to different next calls.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

investmentAccount.description: Only the plans that buy or deliver into this one securities account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_investment_accounts. A plan that only moves money has no securities account and is never returned.

cashAccount.description: Only the plans whose money moves through this one cash account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_cash_accounts - for a plan that buys, its settlement account.

instrument.description: Only the plans that feed this one instrument, as its `uuid` from pp_list_instruments.

tools.name: pp_list_holdings
tools.description:
The statement of assets: everything the file holds on one date and what it is worth, instrument positions and cash account balances in a single list, each with its share of total assets. This is the only place a cash balance can be read and the only place a position's value can be, because the account tools carry neither.

Each position is valued at the most recent price on or before the date, in the instrument's own currency, and that price's own date travels with it. A `priceNote` says when that price needs naming: stale - more than one trading day of the instrument's own calendar passed without a quote, so a weekend or a holiday never counts - or maintained by hand, with its age. Name it when you report a value built on that price. Positions already closed by the date drop out; cash accounts stay in even at zero. A cash account can hold a negative balance - a loan or a credit card - and then has a negative weight, while the others are divided by the smaller net total and can exceed 1; the weights add up to 1 within their rounding to 8 decimals - unless total assets are zero, when every weight is 0.

Without an account parameter this is the whole file, and an instrument held in two investment accounts is a single row. `investmentAccount` or `cashAccount` narrows the report to that one account: the answer then states its `scope` once at the top and gains no column per row, `totalAssets` is that account's value, and every `weight` is the share of it rather than of the file. A scoped report is the shorter answer whenever the question is about one account, and the only way to see where a position sits.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

date.description: Value the file as of this day, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today. A past date gives the statement of assets as it stood then; a future date is accepted and simply uses the latest known prices, which then count as fresh.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings` - the details are on pp_get_overall_performance.

investmentAccount.description: Restrict the report to the positions of this one investment account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_investment_accounts. An account closed by the date is still valued. Its settlement cash is a cash account of its own - named in `scope.referenceCashAccount` - and is not among these rows. Cannot be combined with `cashAccount`.

cashAccount.description: Restrict the report to the balance of this one cash account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_cash_accounts. Cannot be combined with `investmentAccount`.

tools.name: pp_list_taxonomies
tools.description:
The taxonomies of a file: their class trees, the target weight of every class and the vehicles assigned to it. No other tool reaches this: pp_list_holdings says what a position is worth, never which class it belongs to, and pp_get_instrument states master data, never an assignment - so the shape of a portfolio was not answerable.

The answer has two parts. `items` are the taxonomies themselves - always all of them, each with its `classCount` - and `classes` is one flat list of every class, which is what `limit` and `cursor` page through, because a working file holds more classes than fit in one answer. Each class row names the `taxonomy` it belongs to, so a page reads on its own; `taxonomy=<id>` takes one tree instead of all.

Classes arrive in the order the application shows them: a parent before its children, children by `rank`. Every class carries its `parent`, so a page alone is enough to rebuild the tree; `withPath=true` adds the whole `path` of ids from the root, a uuid for every step, and is off by default. **Every ratio is a fraction** - `0.6` is the 60 % the application shows. Two of them mean different things: a class's `targetWeight` is what rebalancing aims at (a class the application creates starts at a whole - `1` - so a weight of `1` marks a fresh class, not a decided one), while an `assignments[].weight` is the factor that class applies to one vehicle's value - `1` counts it in full, `0.6` at 60 % - which is not the slice the class's pie chart draws, since that follows from the value times the factor. A target weight travels exactly as the file stores it: it can exceed a whole, the levels of one tree can sum to far more than a hundred percent, and a negative one can only come from an older version of the application whose dialog still accepted a minus - the current dialog does not. Nothing here is clamped or corrected, because those are the numbers the application itself displays. A taxonomy covers only what is assigned to it: the application's view ends with a row `Ohne Klassifizierung` - unclassified - for the vehicles belonging to no class of that taxonomy, and that row is not a class. It is neither in `items` nor in `classes`, and no `assignedCount` says how much of the file is missing from the tree; the remainder is what is left of pp_list_holdings once the assignments of the taxonomy are subtracted. A file with no taxonomies answers with empty lists. Assignments are off by default, because one class of a working file holds several hundred vehicles: `assignedCount` states the size either way, and `withAssignments=true` is worth sending together with `class` or `limit` - seven classes of a real file carried 838 vehicles between them, which is more than one answer carries. Narrowed to one class and asked for its vehicles, the page moves from the classes to those vehicles: `classes` then holds that one class whole, its `assignedCount` the total in all, while `assignments` is the paged list - in the order of the application's table, with `rank` naming that place on every row, continued with `page.nextCursor` like every other page here. A cursor of the class list is no cursor of the vehicles, and is refused rather than obeyed.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

taxonomy.description: Read one taxonomy instead of all of them, as its `id` from `items`. Unknown here is reported as invalid-value.

class.description: Read one class instead of a whole tree, as its `id`. The way to ask for the vehicles of a single class: together with withAssignments=true this answers that class and all of its vehicles, instead of paging every other class to reach it. A class id is unique within a taxonomy only - without `taxonomy` the id is searched in all of them, and one that several define is refused. Only the class itself comes back, never its subclasses.

withAssignments.description: Whether each class carries the vehicles assigned to it. Off by default: one class of a working file holds several hundred, which is more than one answer holds - `assignedCount` states it either way. Send it together with `class` to read one class and all of its vehicles, or with `limit` to keep the classes few: seven classes of a real file carried 838 vehicles between them.

withPath.description: Whether each class also carries the `path` of ids from the root down to it. Off by default: `parent` already links every class to the one above, and a page is enough to walk the tree, while the path costs one uuid per step - in a working file about half of the whole class list.

cursor.description: Where a page of classes continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before, or a class row's own `cursor`. Only good for the same list, with the same `taxonomy`.

limit.description: At most this many classes; omit it for as many as fit in one answer.

tools.name: pp_assign_vehicle
tools.description:
Puts one vehicle into one class of a taxonomy. A PUT, not a POST: sent twice it has done exactly what it did once, so it can be repeated without doubling anything up. `vehicle` is the uuid of an instrument or of a cash account, as pp_list_instruments and pp_list_cash_accounts give them; an investment account has a uuid too but cannot be placed in a class - assign its reference cash account instead. The class id and the taxonomy it belongs to come from pp_list_taxonomies, and both are asked for, because a class id is only unique inside its own taxonomy.

`weight` is the factor the class's report multiplies the vehicle's value by, as a fraction: `1` counts it in full - which is what every existing assignment of a real file does - and `0.6` counts it at 60 %. Left out, a vehicle newly placed takes `1`, the same as its new class mates; nothing here resets a share silently.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the vehicle and the class: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

taxonomy.description: The taxonomy's `id`, from the `items` of pp_list_taxonomies.

class.description: The class's `id`, from the `classes` of pp_list_taxonomies. Unique only inside the taxonomy named above.

vehicle.description: The uuid of the instrument or cash account to place, from pp_list_instruments or pp_list_cash_accounts. An investment account cannot be assigned and is refused as such.

weight.description: The factor the class applies to the vehicle's value, as a fraction: `1` counts it in full, `0.6` at 60 %. More than 0 and at most 1 - 0 is refused. Omit it to count the vehicle in full, as every existing assignment of a real file does, or to leave an existing factor alone.

tools.name: pp_unassign_vehicle
tools.description:
Takes one vehicle out of one class of a taxonomy. It removes the assignment and nothing else: the instrument or cash account stays in the file, with its bookings and its place in every other taxonomy. The same `taxonomy`, `class` and `vehicle` ids as pp_assign_vehicle.

Refused as `not-assigned` when the class does not hold that vehicle - unlike a missing entity there is nothing to go and look up, so that refusal says the class and the vehicle are both fine and only the relation between them was never there. Sending it twice therefore fails the second time.

A write to a file open in the application: the model changes, the file is marked dirty and the open views recalculate, but nothing is saved to disk and there is no undo - putting it back is pp_assign_vehicle.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the vehicle and the class: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

taxonomy.description: The taxonomy's `id`, from the `items` of pp_list_taxonomies.

class.description: The class's `id`, from the `classes` of pp_list_taxonomies.

vehicle.description: The uuid of the instrument or cash account to take out.

tools.name: pp_update_class
tools.description:
Sets the target weight of one class of a taxonomy - the one number the file keeps that says what a class should be worth, readable since pp_list_taxonomies carried `targetWeight` and untouched by every tool until now.

`targetWeight` is a fraction, the same figure the read gives back: `0.6` is the 60 % the application shows. It may be more than a whole - the classes of one tree need not add up to a hundred percent, and a satellite of 150 % is stored as given - but never negative: a minus came in through an older version of the application whose dialog still accepted one, while the current dialog, like this tool, refuses it.

A class is named by its `class` id from the classes of pp_list_taxonomies and the `taxonomy` whose `items` it belongs to - one class id is unique only inside its own tree. Only targetWeight moves: the name, the parent and the assigned vehicles are what they are, in the application as before.

Setting the same weight again changes nothing - the answer says `changed: false` and leaves the file, unsaved changes included, as it was - so this request may be sent twice.

Before the change is applied the application asks the user, naming the class and the taxonomy it belongs to: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was changed, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

taxonomy.description: The taxonomy's `id`, from the `items` of pp_list_taxonomies.

class.description: The class's `id`, from the `classes` of pp_list_taxonomies. Unique only inside the taxonomy named above.

targetWeight.description: The new target weight as a fraction: `0.6` is the 60 % the application shows. 0 is allowed; more than 1 is stored as given; negative is refused.

tools.name: pp_create_class
tools.description:
Adds one class to one taxonomy - the other half of pp_update_class, which can only move the target weight of a class that already has an id; this one gives the class its id. What the application's `New category` does, given as a name and the parent to hang it under.

`parent` is the id of one class of the same tree, from pp_list_taxonomies; left out, the class hangs under the root. `targetWeight` is the fraction the read gives back - and left out, the class starts at a whole, `1`, exactly as a fresh class of the application does.

The answer carries the class with its new id, which pp_assign_vehicle and pp_update_class accept at once. **A name the parent already carries is refused as `409 name-taken`:** classes do have ids, so two of one name could be told apart - but only by a caller that went and looked, which is the mistake this refuses to let through quietly. Another parent makes another class, and that pair is ordinary: `growth` under `equity` and `growth` under the root are two classes.

Nothing is saved to disk, and there is no undo - this API creates classes and never removes one. Before the class is created the application asks the user, naming the new class and the tree it joins: `403 write-declined` is a no that stands, `423 write-unanswered` means nobody answered within two minutes and nothing was created, and `429 write-pending` means another change is still waiting for an answer. Reads are never asked about.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

taxonomy.description: The taxonomy's `id`, from the `items` of pp_list_taxonomies.

name.description: What the class is to be called. Required in practice although no body property can be declared required: left out, the call is refused naming this field.

parent.description: The id of the class the new one hangs under, from the classes of pp_list_taxonomies. Optional: left out it is the taxonomy's root.

targetWeight.description: The target weight as a fraction: `0.6` is the 60 % the application shows. Optional: left out the class starts at a whole (`1`), as a fresh class of the application does. 0 is allowed; more than 1 is stored as given; negative is refused.

tools.name: pp_get_overall_performance
tools.description:
How the file as a whole performed between two dates: its true time-weighted return, its money-weighted return, and a breakdown of where the change in value came from. This covers everything in the file at once — for the same interval split instrument by instrument, use pp_list_instrument_performance.

The breakdown is a reconciliation rather than a set of totals, and its terms are signed: opening value, unrealized and realized capital gains, income, fees, taxes, currency gains and net deposits add up to the closing value — usually to the cent. First-in-first-out rounding can leave a few cents, and with foreign currencies a larger residual can remain, as in the application's own calculation; the response names any gap above a cent and says which of the two it is. Fees and taxes are negative when they cost money and positive for a refund — the opposite sign to an instrument's `expenses`, which counts charges as positive. Capital gains are stated before fees and taxes, which are terms of their own; taxes are what was booked in the period, not computed from its gains, so they can exceed them. Net deposits is money the user paid in or took out, which is not performance at all — it is in the sum only to make it reconcile, so never present it as a gain.

`irr` is compounded to a year, so over a period of a few days it can be extreme. A period in which the file held nothing at all has no return: `ttwror` and `irr` are then `null`, not 0.

The report is computed for this request and stored nowhere. It has no id, and no figure in it can be fetched back later — identify one by the dates and settings that produced it.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

openingDate.description: Start of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD. A transaction dated on this exact day counts as part of the starting position rather than as activity within the period.

closingDate.description: End of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today, and must be strictly after the opening date. A future date is accepted and values at the latest known prices — it does not forecast: the money figures then include transactions dated after today, while the time-weighted figures stop at today, which the response states as `timeWeightedUntil`. A period that opens today or later has nothing to measure, so its returns are null.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency. Defaults to the file's own base currency. A currency pair the file has no exchange rate series for converts at 1:1, and the response names every such pair in `fxWarnings`; an amount that arrived unchanged and is not named there needed no conversion rather than being refused. Ratios are computed in this currency as well, so a return can differ from what the file's own currency reports - the interval's exchange-rate movements are attributed differently, and the performance shows that part as `currencyGains`, which is zero when the reporting currency is the base currency.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`: the cost basis gains are measured against. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return - the details are on pp_list_trades.

tools.name: pp_list_instrument_performance
tools.description:
How each instrument performed over an interval, one row per instrument, over the same period as pp_get_overall_performance. Its capital gains match the overall report with `taxesAndFees: excluded`; the rows still do not add up to it, because cash accounts, account fees and fees on transfers belong to no instrument. Every instrument the interval touched appears, including one sold during it: that row shows zero shares and a zero closing value but real realized gains, dividends and fees, and leaving it out would quietly erase part of the period.

`irr` and `ttwrorAnnualized` are compounded to a year, so a short period - or a position held only briefly within it - can show an extreme figure; `ttwror` is the plain return over the period. The risk figures need at least two daily returns and are `null` otherwise. `expenses` counts charges as positive and refunds as negative - the opposite sign to the overall report's breakdown.

This is the largest response the API produces and there is no pagination. Narrow `metrics` when a whole file is more than the question needs, or ask about a single instrument with pp_get_instrument_performance.

Every figure is computed for this request and stored nowhere, so a row is reproducible only by asking again with the same dates and settings — the row itself cannot be fetched back.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

openingDate.description: Start of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD; a transaction on this day counts as part of the starting position.

closingDate.description: End of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, after the opening date; defaults to today. For a date in the future see pp_get_overall_performance.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings` - the details are on pp_get_overall_performance.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`: the cost basis gains are measured against. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return - the details are on pp_list_trades.

taxesAndFees.description: `included` (the default) or `excluded`: whether the taxes and fees charged on a purchase or a sale count towards what it cost. It moves cost basis and capital gains together so the two stay comparable, and leaves the fee and tax totals themselves, and every return ratio, alone.

metrics.description:
Which groups of figures to include. Defaults to all seven; an unselected group is simply absent, and a selected one means exactly what it means when all are asked for. An empty list names no group and is refused.

- `valuation` — shares held, opening and closing value, the period's cost basis
- `gains` — realized and unrealized capital gains, each with the part caused by exchange rates
- `income` — dividends received, how many, and the date of the most recent
- `expenses` — the fees and taxes charged, net of refunds: positive, but negative when refunds outweigh charges in the period
- `moneyWeighted` — the annualized internal rate of return
- `timeWeighted` — the true time-weighted return, plain and annualized
- `risk` — volatility, semi-volatility, deepest drawdown, longest drawdown in days

`timeWeighted` and `risk` each need a day-by-day valuation of every instrument in the file, which is what makes this request expensive; the two share that work, so both together cost no more than either alone. The other five are cheap. Narrow this when a response is too large to return whole, and widen it when a figure you need is missing.

tools.name: pp_get_instrument_performance
tools.description:
How one instrument performed over an interval — exactly the row pp_list_instrument_performance would return for it, and nothing about the rest of the file. Cheaper than the collection in substance and not merely narrower, because the day-by-day valuations that `timeWeighted` and `risk` rest on are then computed for this instrument alone.

An instrument that was neither held nor traded in the interval is refused as `no-activity-in-period`: it exists, and the window is empty - widen the period rather than trying another id. `irr` and `ttwrorAnnualized` are compounded to a year, so a short period can show an extreme figure; the risk figures need at least two daily returns and are `null` otherwise.

The figures are computed for this request and stored nowhere; they are reproducible only by asking again with the same dates and settings.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

openingDate.description: Start of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD; a transaction on this day counts as part of the starting position.

closingDate.description: End of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, after the opening date; defaults to today. For a date in the future see pp_get_overall_performance.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings` - the details are on pp_get_overall_performance.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`: the cost basis gains are measured against. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return - the details are on pp_list_trades.

taxesAndFees.description: `included` (the default) or `excluded`: whether the charges on a purchase or a sale count towards its cost. It moves cost basis and capital gains, not the fee and tax totals or any return ratio.

metrics.description:
Which groups of figures to include. Defaults to all seven; an unselected group is simply absent, and a selected one means exactly what it means when all are asked for. An empty list names no group and is refused.

- `valuation` — shares held, opening and closing value, the period's cost basis
- `gains` — realized and unrealized capital gains, each with the part caused by exchange rates
- `income` — dividends received, how many, and the date of the most recent
- `expenses` — the fees and taxes charged, net of refunds: positive, but negative when refunds outweigh charges in the period
- `moneyWeighted` — the annualized internal rate of return
- `timeWeighted` — the true time-weighted return, plain and annualized
- `risk` — volatility, semi-volatility, deepest drawdown, longest drawdown in days

`timeWeighted` and `risk` each rest on a day-by-day valuation, computed here for this instrument alone; the two share that work, so both together cost no more than either alone. The other five are cheap. One instrument is rarely too large to return whole, so ask for what you need rather than trimming.

tools.name: pp_list_transactions
tools.description:
The bookings of a file, one row per transaction as it was recorded: the deposit that funded a purchase, the dividend that arrived, the fee a bank charged, the transfer that moved shares from one securities account to another. Unlike `pp_list_trades`, which reports purchases and sales matched into trades, this reports what was booked - a trade answers how a position did, a transaction answers what happened on a day. Nothing else in this API reaches deposits, removals, interest, fees or transfers.

Rows come back oldest first, and a page belongs to the period it was asked for: carry `page.nextCursor` over only with the same `from` and `to`. `cashAccount`, `investmentAccount` and `instrument` take a uuid. For a purchase or a sale the cash side is the settlement account of the securities account, which the file derives and the booking does not store; a deposit or a fee has no securities side, so asking for an `investmentAccount` never yields one.

A purchase or a sale is **two rows**: one booked in the securities account, with `shares`, `grossAmount` and the charges, and one in the cash account, the money that moved. The two share date, time, amount and note, and `type` is `BUY` or `SELL` in both families - counting rows of that type counts a trade twice. Charges live in two places as well: as the `fees` and `taxes` of a security booking, and as bookings of their own type. One without the other is not the whole bill.

`type` takes the names the `type` field spells, comma-separated and case-insensitive. Cash bookings and security bookings are two families - some names mean the same thing on either side of a transfer, a name of one family simply selects nothing of the other. A transfer appears twice, once in each account it joins, and no row names its counterpart.

`amount` is in the currency of the booking: a file holding foreign positions answers in several currencies at once, and this read has no reporting currency. `grossAmount` comes with a security booking, `fees` and `taxes` only when they are not zero, `shares` only where shares moved.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

from.description: First day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive; a booking on this day is part of the answer. Omit it for no lower bound.

to.description: Last day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, on or after `from`. Omit it for no upper bound.

cashAccount.description: Only bookings with a side in this cash account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_cash_accounts. For a purchase or a sale that is the settlement account of the securities account - `referenceCashAccount` on pp_list_investment_accounts.

investmentAccount.description: Only the bookings of this securities account, as its `uuid` from pp_list_investment_accounts. Deposits, fees and interest are booked in a cash account and never match this filter.

instrument.description: Only bookings naming this instrument, as its `uuid` from pp_list_instruments - a purchase, a sale, a dividend and the fees and taxes attached to them.

type.description: Only these types, comma-separated and case-insensitive: `BUY`, `SELL`, `TRANSFER_IN`, `TRANSFER_OUT`, `DELIVERY_INBOUND`, `DELIVERY_OUTBOUND` for security bookings and `DEPOSIT`, `REMOVAL`, `INTEREST`, `INTEREST_CHARGE`, `DIVIDENDS`, `FEES`, `FEES_REFUND`, `TAXES`, `TAX_REFUND` and the two transfer names for cash bookings. Anything else fails as a field error naming all of them.

cursor.description: Where a page continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before - as on pp_list_instruments.

limit.description: At most this many bookings; omit it for as many as fit in one answer.

tools.name: pp_list_trades
tools.description:
Matched purchases and sales across the whole file, each with its profit and loss, its holding period and its return. Buys are paired against the sells that closed them, so this answers "how did that position actually do" — unlike pp_list_holdings, which values what is held now, and pp_list_instrument_performance, which measures a fixed interval.

A large file has more trades than fit in one answer: narrow it with `from` and `to` to the period the question is about, or to one instrument with pp_list_instrument_trades; what still does not fit comes back one page at a time (`cursor`).

What was sold in a period is `status: ["closed"]` with `from` and `to`, keeping the trades whose `end` lies in it - one sold later was held in the period too. Single purchases and sales are not available here: a trade is their matched result, not a transaction.

A trade has no id. It is recomputed on every call, it cannot be created or edited through this connector, and changing `grouping` or touching the transactions underneath re-cuts it into different trades entirely. Identify one by the filter that produced it; to change one, the user changes its transactions in the application.

Check `direction` before doing arithmetic. On a long trade the profit is exit less entry; on a short one it runs the other way, and since share counts are never negative there is nothing in the figures to tell you which.

The two rates are not the same kind of number: `return` is the gain over the holding period, while `irr` is compounded to a year — a trade held for a few days can show an enormous `irr`, which is the annualization, not a mistake, and for one held only a day or two it often cannot be computed at all and is `null`.

`holdingPeriodDays` is the share-weighted average number of days the shares were held, so with several purchases it is shorter than `end` less `start`. A trade's `note` is the note of its last transaction.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

status.description: `open`, `closed`, or both — the default. A closed trade has been sold out and its result is realized; an open one is still held, so its exit side is a valuation at today's price and the same trade reports different numbers on different days. An empty list names no status and is refused.

grouping.description: `combined` (the default) reports the purchases that one sale closed as a single trade; `per-lot` reports each purchase as a trade of its own. This does not pick a matching strategy — lots are always matched first in, first out.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`. It moves the cost basis that gains are measured against, and with it the split between realized and unrealized gain. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return: `irr` always comes from the actual cash flows — on a trade, those of the lots matched first in, first out, as in the application's own trades view. Under `moving-average` a trade's `irr` can therefore disagree in sign with its `profitLoss`; say which basis each figure is on when you report both. Where the moving average cost is undefined — every short trade — `entryValue`, `profitLoss` and `return` come back `null`, never recomputed some other way.

taxesAndFees.description: `included` (the default) or `excluded`: whether the charges on a purchase or a sale count towards its cost. It moves cost basis and capital gains, not the fee and tax totals or any return ratio.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings` - the details are on pp_get_overall_performance.

from.description: First day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD. Only trades still held on or after it are returned - a trade closed before it is left out. Omit it for no lower bound.

to.description: Last day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD, on or after `from`. Only trades that started on or before it are returned. Together with `from` this keeps the trades held at some point of the period: closed within it, or open through it. Omit it for no upper bound.

cursor.description: Where a page continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before - as on pp_list_instruments.

limit.description: At most this many trades; omit it for as many as fit in one answer.

tools.name: pp_list_instrument_trades
tools.description:
The matched purchases and sales of a single instrument, computed and filtered exactly as pp_list_trades is but scoped to one `uuid`. Use it when the question is about one position rather than the whole file, and to keep a large file's trades down to an answerable size.

An instrument that has simply never been traded answers with an empty list rather than an error. As in the file-wide tool, a trade has no id and is recomputed on every call — identify one by the filter that produced it — and `direction` still decides which way the subtraction runs. `return` is the gain over the holding period; `irr` is compounded to a year, so a trade held for a few days can show an enormous `irr`, which is the annualization rather than a mistake, and one held a day or two often has none (`null`). `holdingPeriodDays` is share-weighted, and `note` is the note of the trade's last transaction.

file.description: The `use` value from pp_list_files, sent exactly as given. Required: there is no default file.

uuid.description: The instrument's `uuid`, from pp_list_instruments. Nothing else resolves: a name, ISIN, WKN or ticker symbol will not.

status.description: `open`, `closed`, or both - the default; as on pp_list_trades.

costMethod.description: `fifo` (the default) or `moving-average`: the cost basis gains are measured against. It never changes `irr` or a time-weighted return - the details are on pp_list_trades.

taxesAndFees.description: `included` (the default) or `excluded`: whether the charges on a purchase or a sale count towards its cost. It moves cost basis and capital gains, not the fee and tax totals or any return ratio.

reportingCurrency.description: Express every amount in this ISO 4217 currency; defaults to the file's base currency. A pair without an exchange rate converts at 1:1 and is named in `fxWarnings` - the details are on pp_get_overall_performance.

from.description: First day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD; keeps the trades still held on or after it, as on pp_list_trades.

to.description: Last day of the period, as YYYY-MM-DD; keeps the trades that started on or before it, as on pp_list_trades.

cursor.description: Where a page continues: `page.nextCursor` of the page before - as on pp_list_instruments.

limit.description: At most this many trades; omit it for as many as fit in one answer.
